title: The Book of Leviticus Timeline
sub: Sacrifice and Holiness · Life at the Foot of the Mountain
desc: Israel's sacrificial system, priestly ordination, dietary law, the Day of Atonement, and the holiness code all unfold in the single year Israel camps at Sinai: grounded throughout in one repeated refrain: be holy, because the LORD your God is holy.

eras.label: Era One · Leviticus 1-3
eras.name: The Burnt, Grain, and Peace Offerings
eras.dates: Three voluntary offerings open the book's sacrificial system: the burnt offering wholly consumed, the grain offering seasoned with salt and never yeast, and the peace offering shared between altar, priest, and worshiper.

events.title: The Burnt Offering: Wholly Given
events.detail: A worshiper lays hands on a flawless animal from herd, flock, or birds, and the entire offering (hide included, for larger animals) is burned completely on the altar as "a gift of a soothing aroma to the LORD," nothing kept back for human use.

events.title: The Grain Offering: Salted, Never Leavened
events.detail: Fine flour, oil, and frankincense make up the grain offering, explicitly forbidden any yeast or honey but required to carry "the salt of the covenant" in every portion: a memorial portion burned on the altar, the remainder belonging to the priests.

verses.text: “You must season every one of your grain offerings with salt; you must not allow the salt of the covenant of your God to be missing from your grain offering.”

events.title: The Peace Offering: Fat for God, Meat to Share
events.detail: The peace-offering sacrifice from herd or flock gives its fat and kidneys to the altar while the meat becomes a shared meal, closing with a permanent prohibition on eating any fat or blood.

eras.label: Era Two · Leviticus 4-5
eras.name: The Sin and Guilt Offerings
eras.dates: Unintentional sin still requires atonement, scaled by who commits it (priest, whole congregation, leader, or ordinary person) with provisions letting the poor substitute birds or even flour when they cannot afford an animal.

events.title: Sin Offerings for Priest, Assembly, Leader, and Individual
events.detail: Unintentional sin requires a sin offering scaled to the offender's status (a bull for the high priest or the whole congregation, a male goat for a leader, a female goat or sheep for an ordinary person) each time followed by the same promise: "the priest will make atonement on his behalf, and he will be forgiven."

verses.text: “The priest will make atonement on their behalf, and they will be forgiven.”

events.title: The Guilt Offering, and Restitution for Deception
events.detail: Specific sins (failing to testify, careless oaths, unwitting contact with uncleanness) require a sin offering that scales down for the poor from a lamb to two birds to a simple grain offering; the guilt offering then addresses trespasses against "the LORD's holy things," and extends to deceiving a neighbor over a pledge or lost item, each requiring restitution plus one-fifth. (Verses 20-26 numbered 6:1-7 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “If he cannot afford an animal from the flock, he must bring… two turtledoves or two young pigeons, to the LORD, one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.”

eras.label: Era Three · Leviticus 6-7
eras.name: Priestly Regulations for the Offerings
eras.dates: A second pass through the same five offerings shifts focus to the priests' own duties (which portions they may eat, where, and under what conditions) closing the book's opening block of sacrificial law. (Hebrew chapter 6 begins at what most English Bibles number as 6:8.)

events.title: The Priests' Portions and Duties
events.detail: Priestly regulations follow for each offering: a perpetual fire that must never go out on the altar, which portions of the grain, sin, and guilt offerings belong to Aaron's sons, and where they must be eaten. (Numbered 6:8-30 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “The fire which is on the altar must be kept burning on it. It must not be extinguished… A continual fire must be kept burning on the altar. It must not be extinguished.” (Numbered 6:12-13 in most English translations.)

events.title: The Guilt and Peace Offerings: Eating Rules and Priestly Shares
events.detail: Detailed rules govern how long peace-offering meat may be eaten before it spoils into uncleanness, permanently forbid eating fat or blood, and assign the priests their specific shares, the wave-offering breast and the contribution-offering thigh, as "a perpetual allotted portion."

eras.label: Era Four · Leviticus 8
eras.name: The Ordination of Aaron and His Sons
eras.dates: Moses personally executes the priestly ordination ceremony detailed earlier in Exodus (washing, vesting, anointing, and blood applied to ear, thumb, and toe) confining Aaron's sons to the tabernacle entrance for a full seven days.

events.title: Moses Ordains Aaron and His Sons
events.detail: Before the whole congregation, Moses washes, vests, and anoints Aaron and his sons, applies blood to their right ear, thumb, and big toe, and confines them to the tabernacle entrance for seven full days "so that you will not die": every step matching what the LORD had commanded Moses in Exodus.

verses.text: “You must reside at the entrance of the Meeting Tent day and night for seven days and keep the charge of the LORD so that you will not die, for this is what I have been commanded.”

eras.label: Era Five · Leviticus 9
eras.name: The First Sacrifices — Fire From the LORD
eras.dates: On the eighth day, Aaron offers his first sacrifices as high priest, and fire bursts from the LORD's own presence to consume the offering: a dramatic confirmation that sends the entire assembly shouting and falling on their faces.

events.title: "Fire Went Out From the Presence of the LORD"
events.detail: Aaron offers sin, burnt, and peace offerings for himself and the people exactly as commanded; after he and Moses bless the assembly, fire goes out from the LORD's presence and consumes the offering on the altar, and the people shout and fall face-down in awe.

verses.text: “Moses and Aaron then entered into the Meeting Tent. When they came out, they blessed the people, and the glory of the LORD [Yahweh] appeared to all the people. Then fire went out from the presence of the LORD [Yahweh] and consumed the burnt offering and the fat parts on the altar, and all the people saw it, so they shouted loudly and fell down with their faces to the ground.”

eras.label: Era Six · Leviticus 10
eras.name: Nadab and Abihu's Strange Fire
eras.dates: The same fire that had just confirmed Aaron's ministry turns deadly the instant his own sons offer unauthorized incense: a sudden tragedy that leaves Aaron silent and reshapes the priestly rules around wine and holy conduct.

events.title: "Among Those Close to Me I Will Show Myself Holy"
events.detail: Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu offer "strange fire" the LORD had not commanded, and fire from the LORD instantly kills them; Aaron responds with silence, and the LORD follows with new rules: no mourning that would disrupt priestly duty, and no wine before entering the tent of meeting, in order to distinguish the holy from the common.

verses.text: “Aaron's sons, Nadab and Abihu… presented strange fire before the LORD [Yahweh], which he had not commanded them to do. So fire went out from the presence of the LORD [Yahweh] and consumed them so that they died before the LORD [Yahweh]. Moses then said to Aaron, ‘This is what the LORD [Yahweh] spoke: “Among the ones close to me I will show myself holy.”’”

eras.label: Era Seven · Leviticus 11
eras.name: Clean and Unclean Animals
eras.dates: Detailed dietary law separates the animal kingdom into edible and forbidden categories (split hooves and cud-chewing for land animals, fins and scales for water creatures) all grounded in the single command to be holy because God himself is holy.

events.title: What Israel May and May Not Eat
events.detail: Land animals must both chew the cud and have a split hoof to be clean, water creatures need fins and scales, and named categories of birds and swarming things are forbidden outright: a dietary code the text grounds not in health but in holiness, echoing the very words later quoted in the New Testament.

verses.text: “I am the LORD [Yahweh] your God [Elohim], and you are to sanctify yourselves and be holy because I am holy… for I am the LORD [Yahweh] who brought you up from the land of Egypt to be your God [Elohim], and you are to be holy because I am holy.”

eras.label: Era Eight · Leviticus 12
eras.name: Purification After Childbirth
eras.dates: A brief chapter sets out the ritual purification period following childbirth, with a shorter timeline after a son than a daughter, closing with the same poverty provision found throughout the sacrificial law.

events.title: A Mother's Days of Purification
events.detail: A woman who bears a son undergoes a shorter purification period than one who bears a daughter, concluding with a burnt offering and sin offering: reduced to two birds for those who cannot afford a lamb.

eras.label: Era Nine · Leviticus 13
eras.name: Diagnosing Skin Disease
eras.dates: An exhaustive diagnostic manual walks the priest through every visual sign that distinguishes a harmless rash from a serious skin disease, extending the same categories even to mold-like infections in fabric and leather.

events.title: The Priest as Diagnostician
events.detail: Priests examine swellings, scabs, and bright spots using precise visual criteria (hair color, depth beneath the skin, spreading over a week's quarantine) to pronounce a person clean or unclean, with the diagnosed required to live outside the camp crying "Unclean! Unclean!"

verses.text: “The diseased person who has the infection… must call out ‘Unclean! Unclean!’ The whole time he has the infection he will be continually unclean. He must live in isolation, and his place of residence must be outside the camp.”

events.title: Disease in Garments and Leather
events.detail: The same diagnostic pattern of examination and seven-day quarantine extends to mold-like infections spreading through wool, linen, and leather, with contaminated items either washed, torn out, or burned depending on severity.

eras.label: Era Ten · Leviticus 14
eras.name: Cleansing From Disease — Including Houses
eras.dates: Recovery from skin disease triggers an elaborate two-stage cleansing ritual involving live birds and cedar wood, and the same diagnostic and purification pattern extends even to houses in the land Israel has not yet entered.

events.title: The Ritual for a Cleansed Person
events.detail: A recovered person undergoes a detailed cleansing ritual (one bird slaughtered, a second released alive over open country) followed by seven days outside the tent, shaving, and a full set of offerings on the eighth day, with the poor again permitted a reduced-cost version.

events.title: Disease in a House
events.detail: In language anticipating life in Canaan, God extends the disease-diagnosis system to houses themselves (quarantined, scraped, or torn down entirely if the infection spreads) with a cleansing ritual for a house that heals, mirroring the ritual for a healed person.

eras.label: Era Eleven · Leviticus 15
eras.name: Bodily Discharges
eras.dates: Regulations on normal and abnormal bodily discharges, for both men and women, establish exactly which contact with a person, their bed, or their seat transmits uncleanness, protecting the tabernacle at the camp's center from defilement.

events.title: Discharges and the Tabernacle's Purity
events.detail: Detailed rules distinguish normal bodily functions from abnormal discharges in both men and women, specifying exactly what becomes unclean through contact and for how long, closing with the stated purpose: "to set the Israelites apart from their impurity so that they do not die… by defiling my tabernacle which is in their midst."

verses.text: “Thus you are to set the Israelites apart from their impurity so that they do not die in their impurity by defiling my tabernacle which is in their midst.”

eras.label: Era Twelve · Leviticus 16
eras.name: The Day of Atonement
eras.dates: Once a year, Aaron alone enters the Most Holy Place behind the curtain to make atonement for the whole nation, including the striking image of a live goat sent into the wilderness carrying Israel's sins away from the camp entirely.

events.title: Aaron Enters the Most Holy Place
events.detail: Following the death of Nadab and Abihu, God gives Aaron strict rules for the one day each year he may enter the Most Holy Place: incense to shield him from the deadly glory, and blood from both a bull and a goat sprinkled on the atonement lid to cleanse the sanctuary itself from Israel's impurities.

verses.text: “Tell Aaron your brother that he must not enter at any time into the Holy Place inside the special curtain in front of the atonement lid that is on the ark so that he may not die, for I will appear in the cloud over the atonement lid.”

events.title: The Scapegoat Sent Into the Wilderness
events.detail: Aaron lays both hands on a live goat and confesses over it all of Israel's sins before it is led away into the desert, bearing their iniquities "into an inaccessible land", establishing the Day of Atonement as a perpetual, once-yearly statute of national cleansing.

verses.text: “Aaron is to lay his two hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the iniquities of the Israelites… The goat is to bear on itself all their iniquities into an inaccessible land, so he is to send the goat away into the desert.”

eras.label: Era Thirteen · Leviticus 17
eras.name: Blood and Sacrifice Centralized
eras.dates: All slaughter must now happen at the tabernacle entrance rather than in the open field, and the underlying theological principle is stated outright: blood makes atonement precisely because it carries the life itself.

events.title: "The Life of the Flesh Is in the Blood"
events.detail: Israelites are forbidden from slaughtering animals anywhere but the tabernacle entrance, preventing sacrifice to "goat demons," and eating blood is banned outright because blood itself carries the life that God has assigned specifically for making atonement on the altar.

verses.text: “The life of the flesh is in the blood, and I myself have assigned it to you on the altar to make atonement for your lives, for the blood makes atonement by means of the life.”

eras.label: Era Fourteen · Leviticus 18
eras.name: Forbidden Sexual Relations
eras.dates: A detailed list of prohibited sexual relationships distinguishes Israel from both Egypt, which they left, and Canaan, which they are entering: framed as the very reason the land itself "vomited out" its previous inhabitants.

events.title: "You Must Not Do as They Do"
events.detail: God explicitly rejects both Egyptian and Canaanite sexual practices, listing forbidden relationships within the family before warning that the land itself became defiled and expelled its former inhabitants for these very things, and will do the same to Israel if they follow suit.

verses.text: “Do not defile yourselves with any of these things, for the nations that I am about to drive out before you have been defiled with all these things. Therefore the land has become unclean, and I have brought the punishment for its iniquity upon it, so that the land has vomited out its inhabitants.”

eras.label: Era Fifteen · Leviticus 19
eras.name: "Be Holy" — the Holiness Code
eras.dates: A sweeping ethical chapter grounds practical commands (honesty, fair wages, care for the poor, impartial justice) in the single repeated refrain "I am the LORD," including the command Jesus would later call the second-greatest commandment.

events.title: "Love Your Neighbor as Yourself"
events.detail: God commands holiness patterned on his own character, then applies it concretely (leaving harvest gleanings for the poor, honest wages, impartial judgment, no slander or hatred) climaxing in the command later quoted by Jesus as the second great commandment.

verses.text: “Speak to the whole congregation of the Israelites and tell them, ‘You must be holy because I, the LORD [Yahweh] your God [Elohim], am holy.’”
“You must not take vengeance or bear a grudge against any of your people, but you must love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD [Yahweh].”

events.title: Mixed Kinds, Honest Measures, and Loving the Foreigner
events.detail: Prohibitions against mixing animal breeds, seed types, and fabrics sit alongside commands to respect the elderly, use honest weights and measures, and "love the foreigner as yourself, because you were foreigners in the land of Egypt."

verses.text: “The resident foreigner who lives with you must be to you as a native citizen among you; so you must love the foreigner as yourself, because you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.”

eras.label: Era Sixteen · Leviticus 20
eras.name: Penalties for Violating the Holiness Code
eras.dates: The offenses named without penalty in chapter 18 receive their legal consequences here, capital punishment for the most severe violations, grounded once more in Israel's calling to be set apart as holy.

events.title: Capital Penalties, and a People Set Apart
events.detail: The sexual and idolatrous offenses catalogued earlier receive their formal legal penalties, most requiring death, with the underlying rationale restated plainly: "I have set you apart from the other peoples to be mine."

verses.text: “You must be holy to me because I, the LORD [Yahweh], am holy, and I have set you apart from the other peoples to be mine.”

eras.label: Era Seventeen · Leviticus 21-22
eras.name: Priestly Purity and Acceptable Offerings
eras.dates: Priests face stricter purity standards than ordinary Israelites (restrictions on mourning, marriage, and physical condition) and every offering brought to the altar must likewise be flawless, since nothing blemished is fit to represent Israel before God.

events.title: Stricter Standards for the Priesthood
events.detail: Priests face special restrictions on mourning contact with the dead and marriage, with even stricter rules for the high priest; a priest with a physical flaw may eat the holy food but cannot serve at the altar, since a flawed offering may not represent the people before God.

events.title: Only Flawless Animals for the Altar
events.detail: Priests in a state of uncleanness are barred from eating holy offerings until purified, and every sacrificial animal must be entirely without blemish: blind, broken, or diseased animals are explicitly rejected, since profaning what is holy profanes the LORD's own name among the people.

eras.label: Era Eighteen · Leviticus 23
eras.name: The Sacred Calendar — Israel's Appointed Feasts
eras.dates: A full liturgical calendar lays out Israel's year around seven appointed times (Sabbath, Passover, Firstfruits, Weeks, Trumpets, the Day of Atonement, and Shelters) each with its own rhythm of rest, offering, and remembrance.

events.title: Passover, Unleavened Bread, and the Firstfruits
events.detail: The weekly Sabbath opens the calendar, followed by Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread, then the wave offering of the first harvest sheaf and, fifty days later, the Feast of Weeks with its firstfruits loaves: the same interval that becomes Pentecost in Acts.

events.title: Trumpets, the Day of Atonement, and Shelters
events.detail: The seventh month brings three appointed times in quick succession: a trumpet-blast memorial, the Day of Atonement with its call to "humble yourselves," and the seven-day Feast of Shelters commemorating Israel's wilderness dwellings, "so that your future generations may know" how God brought them out of Egypt.

verses.text: “The tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. It is to be a holy assembly for you, and you must humble yourselves and present a gift to the LORD [Yahweh].”

eras.label: Era Nineteen · Leviticus 24
eras.name: The Lampstand, the Bread, and the Blasphemer
eras.dates: Instructions for the perpetual lamp and the twelve loaves of the Bread of the Presence are interrupted by a real incident: a man's public cursing of the divine Name, resolved only after Moses seeks a direct ruling from the LORD.

events.title: Continual Oil and Bread Before the LORD
events.detail: Regulations establish a perpetually burning lamp fueled by pure olive oil and twelve loaves of bread arranged weekly before the LORD, belonging afterward to Aaron and his sons as "most holy."

events.title: "An Eye for an Eye": the Blasphemer Stoned
events.detail: A man of mixed Israelite and Egyptian parentage curses the divine Name during a fight, and Moses must seek a direct ruling from the LORD before the whole congregation stones him to death: an incident that becomes the occasion for restating the principle of proportionate justice, "life for life… eye for eye, tooth for tooth."

verses.text: “If a man inflicts an injury on his fellow citizen, just as he has done it must be done to him — fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth.”

eras.label: Era Twenty · Leviticus 25
eras.name: Sabbath Years and the Year of Jubilee
eras.dates: The land itself gets a Sabbath every seventh year, and every fiftieth year brings the Jubilee: a complete economic reset where every Israelite returns to their ancestral property and every enslaved countryman goes free.

events.title: The Land's Sabbath, Every Seventh Year
events.detail: Every seventh year the land itself must rest completely from sowing and harvesting, trusting God's promise of a sixth-year blessing so abundant it covers three years' worth of food.

events.title: The Year of Jubilee: Liberty Proclaimed
events.detail: Every fiftieth year, marked by trumpet blasts on the Day of Atonement, land reverts to its original family and enslaved Israelites go free: a systemic reset grounded in the principle that the land ultimately belongs to God, and Israelites themselves belong only to him, never permanently to one another.

verses.text: “You must consecrate the fiftieth year, and you must proclaim a release in the land for all its inhabitants. That year will be your Jubilee; each one of you must return to his property, and each one of you must return to his clan.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-One · Leviticus 26
eras.name: Blessings and Curses
eras.dates: The covenant's terms are laid out in stark, escalating terms (abundant blessing for obedience, and an intensifying sevenfold series of curses for rebellion) closing, remarkably, with a promise that even after total judgment, God will remember his ancient covenant and not utterly abandon his people.

events.title: Blessing: Rain, Peace, and God's Presence
events.detail: Obedience brings abundant harvests, peace from war and wild animals, victory over enemies, and, climactically, God's own presence walking among them: "I will be your God, and you will be my people."

verses.text: “I will put my dwelling among you, and I will not abhor you. I will walk among you, and I will be your God [Elohim], and you will be my people.”

events.title: Curses Intensifying Sevenfold
events.detail: Disobedience triggers an escalating series of judgments, each stage explicitly "seven times more" than the last (disease and defeat, wild animals, siege and cannibalism, exile among hostile nations) until the land finally gets the Sabbaths it was denied.

verses.text: “If, in spite of all these things, you do not obey me, I will discipline you seven times more on account of your sins.”

events.title: "I Will Remember My Covenant"
events.detail: Even after total judgment and exile, God promises that genuine confession and humbled hearts will move him to remember his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, refusing, even in extremity, to "make a complete end" of his people.

verses.text: “I will remember my covenant with Jacob and also my covenant with Isaac and also my covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Two · Leviticus 27
eras.name: Valuations and Vows
eras.dates: The book closes with practical financial law for converting vows into money (a person's value assessed by age and sex, animals, houses, and land each with their own redemption formulas) and a final reminder that tithes belong to the LORD outright.

events.title: Converting Vows to Silver
events.detail: Detailed valuation tables let a person redeem a vow dedicating themselves, an animal, a house, or land for its assessed silver value plus a fifth, while anything "permanently dedicated" to the LORD, including the tithe of herds and flocks, cannot be redeemed or exchanged at all.

verses.text: “Any tithe of the land, from the grain of the land or from the fruit of the trees, belongs to the LORD; it is holy to the LORD.”
